Emily (Design): quick question — in the rollout wizard how should we surface automatic fallback choices? users are tripping over 'soft degrade' vs 'hard failover' wording :thinking_face:
Matt (Eng): agreed. i think we need clearer affordances. soft degrade = reduced quality but same model, hard failover = switch to cheaper model or cached response
Alyssa (Eng-Platform): +1. also need to show the trigger types next to each option (latency, error-rate, token-cost) so folks don't guess what will flip the switch
Jonah (SRE): we should surface the expected SLO impact and a simple expected RPS change. ops care about blast radius more than the label
Emily (Design): ok so labels + triggers + expected impact. UI idea: three-column compact card per strategy: Label / Triggers (icons) / Quick impact line
Sara (PM): what about an "opt-in" vs "auto" toggle? some customers want to approve every fallback instead of automatic. need to reflect contract differences for Dedicated/Private
Matt (Eng): implementing toggle is fine. but UX needs to explain rollback path and audit trail. if auto fallback flips frequently, we need oscillation mitigation (cooldowns)
Alyssa (Eng-Platform): we currently have a cooldown param in the policy spec. example config snippet i pasted below for clarity:
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  mode: soft_degrade # soft_degrade | hard_failover | cached_response
  triggers:
    - type: latency
      threshold_ms: 1200
    - type: error_rate
      threshold_percent: 5
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  max_consecutive_switches: 2
  audit_log: true
```
Jonah (SRE): that makes sense. audit_log should optionally include sample request/response pairs and model diffs (prompt, tokens, model_id) for debugging
Emily (Design): how verbose should the audit UI be? we can't shove raw pairs by default — maybe an expand/collapse with redaction controls
Sara (PM): default to aggregated metrics + a sample row; for customers with compliance needs, allow full payload with KMS-protected access. also surface "why" for each decision (which trigger fired)
Matt (Eng): we can add a short textual rationale: e.g., "latency spike -> soft_degrade enabled (threshold 1200ms). cooldown in effect: 183s left". that'll help on-call and non-technical PMs
Alyssa (Eng-Platform): telemetry note: we should emit event types: fallback_evaluated, fallback_applied, fallback_reverted, fallback_oscillation_detected. attach policy_id and decision_trace_id
Jonah (SRE): +1, and add sampling flags so heavy traffic customers don't overwhelm the audit store. sample rate should be configurable per workspace
Emily (Design): quick microcopy ask: for soft_degrade do we say "Reduce model quality to preserve latency" or something friendlier?
Sara (PM): "Reduce response richness to meet latency SLOs" maybe. simple and explicit
Matt (Eng): UX edgecase — what if the fallback results in higher error rate? we should show a failure path and auto-unwind if things get worse
Alyssa (Eng-Platform): policy supports revert_on_regression: true/false. default true for hosted, configurable for private
deploy-bot: Rollout 2026-03-15T12:34Z started: canary=5% policy=fallback-v2 (simulated) :white_check_mark:
Jonah (SRE): action items: 1) telemetry events schema (me + Alyssa) 2) small UI mocks for three-card layout (Emily) 3) microcopy options (Sara + Emily) 4) API surface for toggles and audit controls (Matt + Alyssa)
Emily (Design): i'll drop a 3-card mock in #design later today
Alyssa (Eng-Platform): i'll draft the event schema and attach a sample decision_trace payload by EOD
Matt (Eng): i'll add the revert_on_regression flag to the rollout API and wire cooldown counters to the orchestration loop
Sara (PM): perfect. let's aim for a lightweight beta in next sprint. also schedule a 30m sync after mocks landed
Emily (Design): thanks all :tada:
